Content:
In previous lessons, we explored converting larger units of time to smaller ones. In this lesson, we will learn how to convert smaller units of time to larger ones.

Content:
To convert between units of time, we use the following unit conversions:

Content:
- [MATH: 1 \textrm{week} = 7 \,\textrm{days}]
- [MATH: 1 \,\textrm{day} = 24 \,\textrm{hours}]
- [MATH: 1 \,\textrm{hour} = 60 \,\textrm{minutes}]
- [MATH: 1 \,\textrm{minute} = 60 \,\textrm{seconds}]

Content:
Time is typically measured using clocks, and we can use clocks to visualize equivalent units of time.

Content:
For example, the image below shows one complete revolution of the seconds hand on a stopwatch. It takes precisely one minute (or [MATH: 60] seconds) for this hand to complete one full rotation.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/4181e273b49efb25a011f8e57ff24317]

Content:
Let's get some practice at converting between different units of time.

items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose we want to determine how many weeks are in [MATH: 35] days.

Content:
We start with the unit conversion between weeks and days:

Content:
[MATH: 1\, \textrm{week} = 7 \, \textrm{days}]

Content:
Since we wish to convert from days to weeks, we divide both sides by [MATH: 7] and obtain the following:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{1}{7} \, \textrm{weeks} = 1 \, \textrm{day}]

Content:
This equation tells us how many weeks are in [MATH: 1] day. To figure out how many weeks are in [MATH: 35] days, we multiply both sides of the above equation by [MATH: {\color{blue}{35}}{:}]

Content:
[MATH: 35 × (1)/(7)weeks|= 35 × 1day; (35)/(7)weeks|= 35days; (35 ÷ 7)weeks|= 35days; 5weeks|= 35days]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 35] days equals [MATH: 5] weeks.

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
In previous lessons, we explored converting larger units of time to smaller ones. In this lesson, we will learn how to convert smaller units of time to larger ones.

Content:
To convert between units of time, we use the following unit conversions:

Content:
- [MATH: 1 \textrm{week} = 7 \,\textrm{days}]
- [MATH: 1 \,\textrm{day} = 24 \,\textrm{hours}]
- [MATH: 1 \,\textrm{hour} = 60 \,\textrm{minutes}]
- [MATH: 1 \,\textrm{minute} = 60 \,\textrm{seconds}]

Content:
Time is typically measured using clocks, and we can use clocks to visualize equivalent units of time.

Content:
For example, the image below shows one complete revolution of the seconds hand on a stopwatch. It takes precisely one minute (or [MATH: 60] seconds) for this hand to complete one full rotation.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/4181e273b49efb25a011f8e57ff24317]

Content:
Let's get some practice at converting between different units of time.

---

Item 2 — Tutorial: A Worked Example

Content:
Suppose we want to determine how many weeks are in [MATH: 35] days.

Content:
We start with the unit conversion between weeks and days:

Content:
[MATH: 1\, \textrm{week} = 7 \, \textrm{days}]

Content:
Since we wish to convert from days to weeks, we divide both sides by [MATH: 7] and obtain the following:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{1}{7} \, \textrm{weeks} = 1 \, \textrm{day}]

Content:
This equation tells us how many weeks are in [MATH: 1] day. To figure out how many weeks are in [MATH: 35] days, we multiply both sides of the above equation by [MATH: {\color{blue}{35}}{:}]

Content:
[MATH: 35 × (1)/(7)weeks|= 35 × 1day; (35)/(7)weeks|= 35days; (35 ÷ 7)weeks|= 35days; 5weeks|= 35days]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 35] days equals [MATH: 5] weeks.

---

We want to figure out how many weeks are in [MATH: 40] days. So, we multiply both sides of the above equation by [MATH: 40{:}]

[MATH: 40 × (1)/(7)weeks|= 40 × 1day; (40)/(7)weeks|= 40days; 5(5)/(7)weeks|= 40days]

Therefore, [MATH: 40] days equals [MATH: 5\,\dfrac{5}{7}] weeks.
